frequency_question: How often do major partisan voting-reform bills pass the U.S. Senate when one party lacks a filibuster-proof 60-seat majority?
membership_rule: Includes major federal election administration or voter eligibility bills (e.g., NVRA amendments, H.R. 1 / S. 1 equivalents, SAVE Act equivalents) considered in the Senate since 1990 where control was divided or the sponsor lacked 60 votes. Excludes uncontroversial technical corrections or unanimous consent packages.

cases.name: Freedom to Vote Act (S. 1 / S. 2093 equivalents)
Freedom to Vote Act / John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act cloture attempt

coverage_note: 5 major electoral reform vehicles or omnibus attempts tracked since 1990.
known_gaps: Some minor rider amendments attached to appropriations bills are excluded; focusing on standalone or primary omnibus bills.
skeleton: Decomposed into major electoral reform legislative pushes in the Senate under divided or sub-60 majorities.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 5 distinct major legislative attempts = 40% base pass rate under structural friction.
validity_reason: The 60-vote filibuster rule in the Senate remains stable, though procedural threats evolve slowly over decades.
